# Chapter3 Realty

> Chapter3 Realty is a data-forward real estate brokerage serving Myrtle Beach and the Grand Strand region of South Carolina (Horry County). We work with home buyers, sellers, and real estate investors, with a particular specialty in investment-property analysis: long-term rental (LTR) analysis, short-term rental (STR) revenue modeling, DSCR loan qualification, and submarket research across the Grand Strand.

Chapter3 Realty differentiates from other Myrtle Beach brokerages by pairing licensed agents with proprietary investor tools and live market data rather than generic listing search. We provide more property-level intelligence, including rental comps, DSCR and cap-rate math, nearby construction-permit activity, and submarket trends, than is typical for the market.

Full plain-text site content for language models: https://chapter3realty.com/llms-full.txt

## Key facts
- Market served: Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Murrells Inlet, Pawleys Island, Little River, Conway, Carolina Forest, and the wider Grand Strand / Horry County, South Carolina
- Specialties: residential buying and selling, long-term rental investment analysis, short-term rental investment analysis, DSCR loan qualification, submarket research
- Contact: hello@chapter3realty.com | (854) 333-2135
- Service area: Grand Strand, South Carolina
- Last updated: 2026-09-07

## Tools
- [Long-Term Rental Investment Analyzer](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/long-term-rental/): Enter any Grand Strand address and financing terms to get estimated value, market rent, DSCR, cap rate, NOI, cash flow, cash-on-cash return, and appreciation, plus nearby Horry County permit activity.
- [Short-Term Rental Investing in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-tools/): STR revenue, average daily rate (ADR), occupancy analytics, seasonality, and the 90-day mid-term strategy, with live Grand Strand data.

## Invest
- [Investor Hub](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/): Investment-property services and tools for the Grand Strand.
- [STR vs LTR Strategy](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-vs-ltr/): Short-term rental vs. long-term rental strategy for Myrtle Beach.
- [Are Myrtle Beach Condos a Good Investment?](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/condos/): Condo investing on the Grand Strand, including HOA fees, insurance, and financing considerations.
- [Condotel Financing in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/condotel-financing/): How condotel and non-warrantable condo loans work, typical down payments, and why most banks decline these buildings.
- [Non-Warrantable Condos in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/non-warrantable-condos/): What makes a condo non-warrantable, the loans that finance one, the Fannie Mae master-insurance rule flagging coastal buildings, and how to check a building before you make an offer.
- [Short-Term Rental Rules by City](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-rules/): Where STRs are legal in Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Surfside, unincorporated Horry, Conway, and Pawleys Island, with licenses and the 11-13% tax stack. Verified July 2026.
- [Accommodations Tax & Business License by Jurisdiction](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/accommodations-tax/): What a Grand Strand rental owes: 5% sales plus 2% state accommodations tax, Horry County hospitality fee at 3% outside city limits and 1.5% inside, Georgetown County 3%, Conway 1%. The transient threshold is 90 days everywhere except Georgetown County, which is 30. Business license renews April 30 and is priced on gross rent. Verified September 2026.
- [Short-Term Rental Tax Treatment & the Participation Test](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-tax-treatment/): The seven-day average stay rule that takes a property out of the rental-activity definition, the seven material participation tests with their hour thresholds, what counts as participation, and what records are accepted. Explains why Grand Strand management companies and condotel rental pools cut against the hour tests. Teaches the test; does not apply it. Verified September 2026.
- [Cost Segregation on a Beach Condo & Recapture](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/cost-segregation/): What a study reclassifies in a furnished condo (carpet, appliances, furniture to 5-year; structure stays at 27.5), the 100 percent special depreciation allowance for property acquired after January 19, 2025, why the passive loss rules decide whether the loss is usable, and the two recapture layers at sale: ordinary income on reclassified personal property, up to 25 percent on the building. Verified September 2026.
- [Depreciating a Myrtle Beach Rental from Closing Day](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/rental-depreciation/): Which closing costs go into basis and which stay out, splitting the price between land and building using the Horry County assessment record, placed in service and the mid-month convention, repairs against improvements and the de minimis safe harbor, and the allowed-or-allowable rule at sale. Verified September 2026.
- [The 14-Day Rule and Using Your Own Beach Condo](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/14-day-rule/): Personal use of more than the greater of 14 days or 10 percent of fair-rental days makes the unit a home; what counts as a personal day (family, below-market guests, swaps; repair days excluded); the fewer-than-15-days rule; expense allocation by days; the income ceiling and ordering. Distinguishes this count from the 4 percent property-tax day count, the 90/30-day accommodations-tax thresholds and the seven-day average. Verified September 2026.
- [Run the Numbers on a Myrtle Beach Rental](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/run-the-numbers/): a free request form. Send one address and a plan; a licensed team member returns rent, property tax at the 6 percent rate, insurance, HOA dues, management and monthly cash flow the same day, with the rental rules at that address and whether lenders finance the building. Estimates for a buying decision, not an appraisal or a loan quote. Verified September 2026.
- [Buying a Myrtle Beach Rental From Out of State](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/out-of-state/): how a remote buyer closes without visiting. South Carolina requires an attorney to supervise the closing; the buyer signs by mail before a notary in their own state with two witnesses, or by power of attorney; South Carolina notary law does not allow video notarization; wire fraud is avoided by phone verification on a known number; property tax at 6 percent; flood coverage starts at a loan closing but 30 days after purchase for a cash buyer; utilities by area. Verified September 2026.
- [Property Management in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/property-management/): what a manager costs and what to ask. South Carolina requires a real estate or property manager license under a manager-in-charge; tenant deposits stay in a trust account until the lease ends; deposit deductions must be itemized within 30 days with a three-times penalty; the written management agreement must state fees, renewal terms and cannot bind a future sale listing; who remits accommodations tax and the Horry County hospitality fee when a manager books the stay. No local fee average exists. Verified September 2026.
- [Rental Program vs Airbnb for a Myrtle Beach Condo](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/rental-program-vs-airbnb/): the building rental desk against self-managing on Airbnb or Vrbo. Airbnb host fee 3 percent (15.5 percent host-only for software users), Vrbo 5 percent plus 3 percent; whoever takes the payment remits the state accommodations tax; Horry County hospitality fee 3 percent outside city limits and 1.5 percent inside; program agreements can cap owner use and make the building a hotel-type project for lenders; what to read in the agreement and the owner statement. Verified September 2026.
- [Cash to Close on a Myrtle Beach Rental](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/cash-to-close/): every line an investor pays beyond the down payment at a Horry County closing. The attorney runs the closing under state law; the lender policy is required and the owner policy optional; the seller pays the deed recording fee except on foreclosure, government and retirement-plan deeds; a year of insurance and the tax escrow are prepaid; Horry County bills October 1 and payment is due January 15; lender reserves are measured in months of the full monthly cost, six months being common for a rental; state retail license $50; county business license $55 minimum plus $1.37 per $1,000, doubled for a business with no fixed place in the county. No loan terms stated. Verified September 2026.
- [Where to Buy a Rental on the Grand Strand](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/where-to-buy/): nine areas in one table for a rental investor: county (Murrells Inlet, Litchfield and Pawleys Island are Georgetown County), whether nightly rentals are allowed (Myrtle Beach only in marked zones and never in R districts, with a December 2024 overlay barring 90-day-plus leases in oceanfront short-term buildings; North Myrtle Beach no special zoning; Surfside Beach under-30-day stays only in R3 and C3; unincorporated Horry County no county rule, covenants decide; Georgetown County tourist homes up to 30 days in resort districts; Conway commercial short-term rental in three downtown districts), the license body and year, and local levies on top of the state 7 percent. Georgetown County uses a 30-day tax threshold, Horry County 90 days. Verified September 2026.
- [Myrtle Beach Short-Term Rental Setup After Closing](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/str-setup/): the eight steps after closing in order: zoning and covenants, the city or county business license (Myrtle Beach every rental, renewals due April 30; North Myrtle Beach all STRs; Horry County unincorporated May 1 to April 30, class 6 at $55 minimum plus $1.37 per $1,000; Georgetown County none), the $50 state retail license only for direct bookings, the state 5 plus 2 percent and the county 3 or 1.5 percent hospitality fee due the 20th, city levies, what Airbnb collects, the county personal property return on furnishings, alarms under the 2021 codes, landlord insurance, listing rules, utilities, Schedule E and the 1099-K threshold. Verified September 2026.
- [Mid-Term Rentals in Myrtle Beach: The 90-Day Floor](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/mid-term-rentals/): furnished stays of one to six months. A stay of 90 continuous days pays no state accommodations tax and no Horry County hospitality fee, and the City of Myrtle Beach does not count it as a short-term rental, so a 90-day lease is legal in residential zones where nightly rentals are banned; the floor inside the city is 90 nights, not 30; the December 2024 oceanfront overlay bars 90-day-plus leases in short-term buildings of more than two units; Surfside Beach defines transient as under 30 days. Travel nurse contracts are 13 weeks; the Grand Strand hospitals; the federal lodging rate for Horry County ($110, $132 and $182 by season, FY2026); Furnished Finder ($199 a year, no commission) and Airbnb monthly stays (28 nights). Verified September 2026.
- [Student Rentals Near Coastal Carolina University](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/student-rentals/): buying a rental for Coastal Carolina University students in Conway. The university had 12,006 students in fall 2025; first- and second-year students must live on campus, so tenants are juniors, seniors and graduate students; fall 2026 classes run August 19 to December 11, spring January 11 to May 4, fall move-in August 12 to 16; the City of Conway defines a family as up to three unrelated people; the CCU Neighborhood Overlay (Quail Creek, Quail Creek Village, College Park, College Place, Barberry Drive) caps unrelated occupants at the bedroom count on the county record, never more than four, with no street or yard parking 11pm to 8am; unincorporated Horry County allows five unrelated; the university's 2026-27 off-campus housing allowance is $8,086 for the academic year. About three in four student leases carry a parent co-signer (Chapter3 files); Chapter3 recommends tenants who earn three to five times the rent. Federal fair market rents for Horry County, FY2027: $1,155 studio, $1,258 one bedroom, $1,504 two, $1,823 three, $1,981 four (40th percentile gross rents, county-wide, not student rents by the room). Verified September 2026.
- [Section 8 Rentals in Horry County, SC](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/section-8-rentals/): renting to Housing Choice Voucher tenants. Two authorities run the program: the Housing Authority of Myrtle Beach (660 vouchers, eastern Horry County) and the Conway Housing Authority (373, Conway and the unincorporated county). The authority pays its share by direct deposit monthly up to a payment standard of 90 to 110 percent of the fair market rent, which is $1,981 for four bedrooms in FY2027; the standard used is the lower of the voucher's and the unit's bedroom count. Inspection within 15 days, contract within 60 days of the lease, no payment before it. Damage beyond wear can end the family's assistance; eviction for a serious lease violation must; a new voucher can be refused for five years after such an eviction.
- [Renting Out New Construction on the Grand Strand](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/new-construction-rentals/): 6,898 homes authorized in 2025 and 7,152 in 2024 in the Myrtle Beach area. Whether a new house can be rented depends on the recorded covenants, and an association rule is enforceable only if recorded with the county (SC Code 27-30-130). In Chapter3's files the early buyers in a new community get the lowest price and the cash flow; in one Little River community townhouses rented a little over $2,000 while the price went from $230,000 to $292,000 in about eighteen months. Builders give incentives to FHA, VA and conventional buyers, rarely to investor loans.
- [Financing Your Second, Third and Fourth Rental](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/financing-multiple-rentals/): standard loans allow ten financed properties per borrower, counting a financed primary home; reserves are six months on the new investment property plus 2, 4 or 6 percent of the other financed balances by count. Rent counts toward qualifying income only after twelve months of managing property, which is why the first rental is the hardest to finance; investor lenders often want experience. A cash-out refinance or a line of credit on a property you own can fund the next down payment, and both loans then depend on the rents.
- [Landlord Insurance on a Myrtle Beach Rental](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/landlord-insurance/): a rental needs a landlord policy, wind coverage on most of the coast, and flood where the zone or the lender requires it. The insurance trade body puts a landlord policy at about 25 percent more than a homeowner policy; in Chapter3's files 15 to 20 percent. Federal flood insurance charges a rental a $250 yearly surcharge instead of $25. The larger cost is property tax: a rental at 6 percent with the school operating tax pays three to four times the bill of the same house as a legal residence, and taxes end more deals here than insurance.
- [Myrtle Beach Rent Prices: What a House Rents For](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/rent-prices/): the FY2027 fair market rent for Horry County is $1,155 studio, $1,258 one bedroom, $1,504 two, $1,823 three, $1,981 four, the 40th percentile of gross rents with utilities; the metro's typical asking rent was about $1,714 in July 2026 and $1,695 in September 2025. Bedroom count, location, condition, furnishing and lease length move one house above or below those. The site's analyzer estimates rent for any address; an agent runs it from local leases before an offer.
- [South Carolina Landlord Rules and Evictions](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/landlord-rules/): the deposit is itemized and returned within 30 days of move-out, or the landlord owes three times the amount wrongfully withheld; the owner's name and address go to the tenant in writing at move-in; 24 hours notice to enter; rent unpaid five days after the due date allows termination when the lease carries the state's bold notice clause; 14-day cure notice for other breaches; 30 days written notice ends a month-to-month tenancy; retaliation barred for 75 days after a complaint; Horry County eviction: sworn Application for Ejectment (SCCA 732) at the magistrate court for the property's area, rule to vacate served in person (10 days to answer) or posted and mailed (20 days), writ within five days of a win, the sheriff gives 24 hours; statewide magistrate fee schedule $55 with the $20 filing fee rising to $40 on January 1, 2027; a lockout costs three months of rent or twice the damages; magistrate money limit $7,500; six magistrate offices (Conway, Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Little River, Loris, Aynor); a servicemember cannot be evicted without a court order when rent is at or below $10,542.60 a month in 2026. Chapter3's observed Horry County timeline: up to three weeks from filing to the writ, a few days for a strong case. Selling the house is not a ground for ejectment; a month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days written notice; an all-inclusive property manager handles the eviction, a manager paid for some services does not. Verified September 2026.
- [Buying a Myrtle Beach Rental in an LLC](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/llc/): $110 to file articles of organization ($15 online records charge), a registered agent with a South Carolina street address, no annual report or license fee for an LLC not taxed as a corporation; a deed from a member to a single-member LLC ignored for tax owes no deed recording fee and is not an assessable transfer, so the property tax value does not reset; a multi-member LLC is exempt only when the contribution is tax-free under the federal partnership rule; selling more than half of the LLC later is an assessable transfer with a 45-day notice duty; income tax unchanged (Schedule E for a single-member LLC, a partnership return for two or more members); conventional loans are made to natural persons, the federal due-on-sale exemption list names no LLC, many servicers allow a post-closing transfer to a borrower-controlled LLC and require the deed back before a refinance, DSCR loans close in the LLC's name; the state supreme court (CFRE, 2011) held a single-member LLC-owned home can take the 4 percent legal residence rate; nonresident withholding at the top individual rate (5.21 percent for a 2026 sale) for a partnership-taxed LLC and 5 percent for a corporation-taxed one. Every Chapter3 investor client holds title in an LLC, a trust or a corporation; every DSCR and business-purpose loan closes in the entity and the lender requires it (a loan officer at our preferred lender). Moving a house financed as a primary residence into an LLC and renting it a month after closing breaks the occupancy promise and is mortgage fraud. On a multi-member LLC the 4 percent rate is prorated to the resident member's share, with two statutory exceptions (a quarter interest with immediate family; an LLC of the resident and immediate family only). Verified September 2026.
- [Buying a Foreclosure in Horry County, SC](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/foreclosures/): the master-in-equity sale is held at 11am on the first Monday of each month (Tuesday after a holiday) on the third floor of 1301 2nd Avenue, Conway; new bidders register at least a week ahead with a photo ID and no one registers on sale day; in-person bidding only in $500 increments; a first-time winner brings a $2,500 certified check to the close of bidding, every winner pays 5 percent of the bid in certified funds by noon the next day and the balance within 30 days, or forfeits the deposit and future bidding rights; when a deficiency judgment is demanded the bidding stays open 30 days and reopens at 11am on the 30th day, and the lender cannot bid again; the master's deed carries no warranty, passes only what the court adjudged, and is subject to taxes and to liens of anyone not in the case (Ex parte Johnson, 2006); the buyer pays the deed recording fee on a master-in-equity deed; a bona fide tenant keeps the lease or gets 90 days notice under federal law; HUD homes give owner-occupants an exclusive period of 15 days (insured) or five days (uninsured) and take offers only through HUD-registered brokers; the county tax sale (taxes delinquent March 17, sale advertised in November, cash or certified funds, $25 registration, $450 title and deed charge) carries a 12-month redemption period during which the bidder has no rights to the property. Tim Nash has bought at the sale many times, for himself and for clients. Tax sale: only the owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem, and redemption returns the house to the owner; the county mails certified notice 20 to 45 days before the redemption year ends and can void a sale for a missed step (a Chapter3 client got his bid back with interest that way); a tax deed is evidence of title, contestable for two years after the sale. REO earnest money is held by the closing attorney, and a loan on a bank-owned purchase is about 45 days (Chapter3's files). Past-due HOA assessments on a foreclosed condo are checked before closing. Verified September 2026.
- [Myrtle Beach Market Report, July 2026](https://chapter3realty.com/market-reports/july-2026/): June 2026 sales, prices, inventory, permits, and mortgage rates for the Grand Strand, with sources.
- [How Much Do Airbnbs Make in Myrtle Beach?](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/airbnb-income/): 2026 income data from five vendors ($22.6k-$42k gross average), by area and percentile, with gross-to-net worked examples and the condotel management-split math.
- [Myrtle Beach Oceanfront Condo Building Directory](https://chapter3realty.com/invest/condo-buildings/): 29 buildings with rental operations, published HOA fees ($300-$1,900/mo), price bands, and how lenders decide which buildings finance.

- [Getting Around Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/getting-around/): the airport's airlines and nonstop cities, the two US 17s explained, the SC-31 and SC-22 freeways locals use, the Coast RTA bus, golf carts, day trip drive times, and the honest status of I-73.
- [Moving From Virginia to Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-virginia/): the one state where the annual car tax is already familiar, the $12,000 age deduction that phases out dollar for dollar above $50,000 AGI, the $40,000 military subtraction against South Carolina's uncapped exemption, and prices compared.
- [Moving From Connecticut to Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-connecticut/): property tax from 1.54 percent effective to about 0.38 on a primary home, the AGI cliffs Connecticut draws on Social Security and pension income, benefit recapture, the capped car tax that usually shrinks here, and the gift tax that now reaches almost nobody.
- [Moving From Massachusetts to Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-massachusetts/): the $2 million estate tax threshold left behind, the warning that Massachusetts public pensions are taxed in South Carolina, the 5 percent flat tax against ours, the halved car excise, and a typical house for close to half.
- [Moving From Florida to Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-florida/): what a Florida sale buys here, a smaller beach town that keeps ten airlines and six hospitals, day-to-day prices under the Florida average, the insurance quotes to get before any offer, and the honest tax section where most lines rise a little.
- [Grand Strand Beach Rules by Town](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/beaches/): the dog clock beach by beach including Pawleys Island's year-round allowance, umbrella and tent limits by jurisdiction, resident parking decals, and the November through February golf cart season on the county's unincorporated beaches.
- [Retirees](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/retirees/): Buying for retirement on the Grand Strand, 55-plus options.
- [Common Buyer Mistakes](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/common-mistakes/): Mistakes Grand Strand buyers make and how to avoid them.
- [Can You Buy a Condo in Litigation?](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/condo-in-litigation/): Whether you can buy a Grand Strand condo in active litigation, why lenders decline it, and a real deal where it became the buyer’s best discount.
- [How to Find Out If a House Flooded](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/undisclosed-flooding/): Flood zone vs flood history, how to uncover a home's real flood record before buying, and a Grand Strand case where undisclosed flooding surfaced.
- [Horry County Property Taxes: 4% vs 6%](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/property-taxes/): The legal residence rate vs the second-home and investment rate, Act 388, the Homestead Exemption, worked examples, and a calculator.
- [Coastal Home Insurance Costs](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/coastal-insurance/): The three policies coastal owners carry, hurricane deductibles in dollars, flood zone myths, and how to pay less.
- [SC Closing Costs Calculator](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/closing-costs/): Buyer and seller closing costs in South Carolina: deed stamps ($1.85/$500), attorney-state fees, title rates, Horry County escrow math, VA fee rules, with an interactive calculator.
- [55+ Communities in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/55-plus-communities/): Nine verified communities compared: prices from $190k, HOA fees $43-$384/mo, the land-lease model, CCRCs, and SC retiree tax breaks.
- [Golf Course Communities in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/golf-communities/): 14 communities compared: membership required vs optional vs public, HOA fees from $35/mo, Barefoot's $2,750 transfer fee, and flood-zone cautions.

## Sellers
- [Sellers Hub](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/): Selling a home in Myrtle Beach with data-driven pricing.
- [What Is My Home Worth in Myrtle Beach?](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/home-value/): Free CMA from a licensed Grand Strand broker: how the number is built from sold comps and what actually moves a home's value here.
- [Cost to Sell a House in South Carolina](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/net-proceeds/): Seller net proceeds calculator: commission, deed stamps at $1.85 per $500, attorney fees, and the walk-away number.
- [For Sale By Owner in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/fsbo/): What SC law requires from FSBO sellers, the NAR price data ($360k FSBO vs $425k agent-listed median), flat-fee FSBO coaching credited back if you hire us, and what full service includes.
- [Selling to Out-of-State Buyers](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/out-of-state-buyers/): Reaching the out-of-state buyers who drive Grand Strand demand.
- [Selling an Inherited House in South Carolina](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/inherited-house/): Probate timing, the stepped-up basis, the property tax jump, and the three ways to sell an inherited property.
- [Selling a Condo in Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/sell-my-condo/): 2026 condo market data (137 DOM, 7.6 months supply), pricing to the building's real buyer pool, SC booking-transfer law, and HOA document fees.
- [Capital Gains Tax Selling a House in SC](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/capital-gains/): The 44% SC gain deduction (~2.92% effective for 2026), federal brackets, and the I-290/I-295 nonresident withholding every out-of-state seller hits, with a calculator.
- [Selling a Myrtle Beach Rental With Tenants in Place](https://chapter3realty.com/sell/rental-property/): the lease continues and the buyer becomes the landlord at closing; the seller stays liable for the security deposit until it is transferred to the buyer and the tenant is told in writing; showings on 24 hours notice at reasonable times; a vacation rental transfers subject to every booking that starts within 90 days of the deed being recorded and to the management agreement for those stays, later guests are refunded within 45 days, and every future booking must be disclosed in writing before the contract; the state disclosure statement must say whether a lease or rental management agreement will be in place at closing; a nonresident seller is withheld at the state's top individual rate (6 percent for a 2025 sale, 5.21 percent for 2026) on the gain with a signed I-295 affidavit or on the whole amount realized without one, 5 percent for a corporation; depreciation is recaptured at up to 25 percent; a 1031 exchange identifies within 45 days and closes within 180. An FHA buyer must move in within 60 days of closing, so a lease with more than three to four months left means an investor buyer, a wait, or a paid buyout (a loan officer at our preferred lender). Selling is not a ground for ejectment; a month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days notice. The seller stays liable for the deposit until it is transferred to the buyer and the tenant is told in writing. A house the tenant kept up sells to a turnkey investor; a damaged one sells to a value-add investor for less. Verified September 2026.

- [HOA vs POA vs Condo Regime](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/hoa-vs-poa/): What you own, who insures what, and why regime fees are not comparable to HOA dues.
- [Condo master insurance vs HO-6](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/master-insurance-ho6/): where the association's policy stops and your HO-6 starts, and who pays the deductible.
- [Who pays when a condo is damaged](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/who-pays-for-damage/): a leak from the unit above, a roof, a burst pipe, and what decides responsibility.
- [How much can an HOA raise dues](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/dues-increases/): what South Carolina law requires, and what actually limits an increase.
- [HOA violations and fines in South Carolina](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/violations-and-fines/): what the enacted law does and does not provide, and where an association's power comes from.
- [HOA estoppel letters and transfer fees](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/estoppel-and-transfer-fees/): the HOA line items at closing, and why unpaid dues follow the unit.
- [Buying into a developer controlled HOA](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/developer-control-turnover/): South Carolina sets no turnover rule, and dues often jump afterwards.
- [Are HOA fees tax deductible](https://chapter3realty.com/hoa/tax-deductible/): the answer differs for a home you live in, one you rent, and one you do both with.

## Submarkets
- [Submarket Index](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/): Compare Grand Strand submarkets for buying and investing.
- [Carolina Forest](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/carolina-forest/): The area's biggest master-planned community: 26,000+ residents, medians near $418k-$465k, top-ranked schools, no city tax, no wind-pool surcharge, 11 subdivisions compared.
- [Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/myrtle-beach/): The core Grand Strand market: deepest condo inventory, resort zones that allow short-term rentals, inland single-family neighborhoods.
- [North Myrtle Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/north-myrtle-beach/): Family-beach STR market, medians roughly $399k-$415k, short-term rentals allowed citywide with a licensing ordinance pending.
- [Surfside Beach](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/surfside-beach/): Small family beach town; short-term rentals limited to two zoning districts; oceanfront medians into the $800ks, typical values near $347k-$360k.
- [Garden City](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/garden-city/): Unincorporated beach community, STR-permissive with no city ordinance; days on market near 162 favor buyers.
- [Murrells Inlet](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/murrells-inlet/): MarshWalk dining economy on a split Horry/Georgetown county tax map; slower market times favor patient buyers.
- [Pawleys Island](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/pawleys-island/): Upscale south end, median list prices mid-$500ks, no short-term rental regulation, second-home driven.
- [Little River](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/little-river/): Boating and fishing end of the Strand, medians near $292k, more affordable than the oceanfront towns.
- [Conway](https://chapter3realty.com/submarkets/conway/): Inland value market, medians near $280k, the lowest entry prices in Horry County, steady long-term rental demand.
